# Pass 1

Reviewer pass on `units.json` (25 units, 320–370). `t` untouched in all units (checked before and after by script); JSON valid; 18 units changed, 48 change entries. Order followed: labels and positions, OE to `l`, `l` to `i`, remembered English, consistency with published parts.

Totals: **high 4, medium 19, low 25.**

## Changes

### High

- **321 · n · high.** Said the 323b variant ‘furður’ was in "the transcript Thorkelin made in 1787". The apparatus abbreviation is ‘Tr.’, which is Trautmann (the same apparatus cites ‘Tr. Bonn. B.’ and ‘Tr.1 127’; Thorkelin is ‘Thk.’). Also said Klaeber prints ‘furðum’ "as the better sense", which the apparatus does not say. Now: the apparatus records ‘furður’ from Trautmann (‘Tr.’), Klaeber prints ‘furðum’.
- **356 · n · high.** Same misattribution at 357a: "Thorkelin's transcript (with a query)". Now credits Trautmann (‘Tr.’, once with a page reference and a query), Holthausen and Chambers.
- **358 · n · high.** Labelled ‘Deniga freân’ a dative, "before the lord of the Danes". ‘for’ already governs the dative ‘eaxlum’; ‘freân’ (weak noun, -an serves for gen., dat., acc.) is a genitive depending on ‘eaxlum’, as the unit's own `l` has it ("before the shoulders … of the Danes' lord"). Rewritten as a genitive. Glossary follow-up: the shared entry for ‘freân’ lists only the dative; a `__broaden__` for the genitive is needed in the glossary step (not edited here).
- **350 · l · high.** "as you petitioners are": ‘þū’ and ‘bēna’ are both singular. Now "as you a petitioner are".

- **325 · i.** "hard beyond breaking" adds a meaning the compound does not give. Now "exceedingly hard".
- **328 · n.** Last sentence asserted the spears "are leaned against the wall"; the text says only ‘stōdon’. Sentence deleted.
- **331 · n (speaker).** "I take him to be the speaker" hedged a point the text settles: Wulfgār answers the Geat leader's reply at 348, so he is the questioner, and 335 has him call himself Hrothgar's ‘ār ond ombiht’. Rewritten as that reasoning; the poem is said not to name him here. Unit 348's last sentence ("He is the man who questioned the Geats at 331") now carries the same reasoning (see 348).
- **331 · n (line 392).** "which I take to use the same phrase": line 392 in the source reads ‘þæt hē ēower æþelu can’, the same noun. Now says so.
- **338 · n.** The last sentence named Beowulf ("and Beowulf answers") before the poem does (343) and against unit 340's note ("The poem has not yet named the speaker"). Now "the Geat leader answers in the next unit".
- **338 · i.** "greatness of spirit" is a stock rendering of ‘higeþrymmum’ (echo risk). Rebuilt: "pride and strength of mind".
- **344 · l.** ‘hine’ dropped: "that we so good a one greet may". Now "that we him, so good a one, greet may."
- **344 · l.** "to your elder" for ‘aldre’; the same word is "chief" in `l` and note at 369. Now "to your chief" (note adjusted to match).
- **344 · n (Lang. § 18.2).** "which I have not seen" is a reviewer's confession in a published note, and "Klaeber keeps the manuscript's ‘sunu’" is not in the apparatus. Now: Klaeber prints ‘sunu’; the apparatus sends the reader to ‘Lang. § 18.2’, which the transcription does not include, so his reason is not known here. Published notes use no editorial "I".
- **344 · n (mōton).** "a subjunctive of polite request": ‘mōton’ is the present plural of ‘mōtan’ (the subjunctive plural would be ‘mōten’). Now labelled as the present plural, "may, be allowed".
- **348 · i.** ‘wīg’ ("war") dropped: "his courage and wisdom". Now "his spirit was known to many, in war and in wisdom".
- **348 · n (identification).** See 331; last sentence now gives the grounds.
- **350 · i.** "about this … about your journey" doubled the anticipatory ‘þæs’ and left "that famous prince" stranded. Reordered: "…the giver of rings, that famed lord, about your journey, as you request, and will soon make known…".
- **350 · n.** "‘wine’, ‘friend’, a genitive plural ‘Deniga’" read as if ‘wine’ were the genitive plural. Now: ‘wine’ accusative singular, ‘Deniga’ genitive plural.
- **358 · i.** "face to face" is an interpretation presented as a translation. Now "stood close before the lord of the Danes".
- **361 · l.** "come-together" for ‘geferede’ contradicts the note ("journeyed", from ‘gefēran’). Now "journeyed".
- **364 · n (mōton).** "a plural subjunctive of ‘mōtan’": same fix as 344.
- **368 · n (T.C. § 23).** "Klaeber's textual notes (T.C. § 23)" asserted what the section is. Now: a numbered section the transcription does not include; the apparatus cites it again at 395b ("Cf. T.C. § 28, also § 23") for the same -getāwum/-geatwum pair, which is checkable in the source.
- **369 · i.** "a man of worth" is too close to a well-known rendering of ‘dēah’ here. Rebuilt: "and truly the chief is a worthy man".

## Considered and refused

- **Speaker at 331–339.** Kept as Wulfgār, now argued from the sequence (348 reply, ‘ār ond ombiht’ at 335) instead of hedged with "I take". No further hedge: the dialogue structure makes it near-certain, and the note says the poem does not name him at 331.
- **Dot under the vowel at 336.** Earlier parts explain it first in fitt-03 (190, 219), but the convention is to explain it the first time each part meets one, and this is the only dotted vowel in this part. Kept; wording matches fitt-03's.
- **Demonstratives in 333 `i`** ("these … shields", "this heap of spears"). Not in the Old English, but natural spoken deixis for men standing in front of the speaker. Kept.
- **‘fǣtte’ "from a word for a plate of metal".** Cannot be checked against a lexicon in this pass; it is already marked as a guess. Left.
- **Unit 320 `i` "paved with stones of many colours".** The note already says the picture is a guess and ‘stānfāh’ may mean only ‘stony’. Left.
- **‘eorla’ as "earls" (356, `l` 368) and "nobles" (`i` 368).** Both are in the glossary entry ("nobles, warriors"); fitt-03 247 also varies. Left.
- **‘þæt’ as "until" at 358.** A result/extent clause; "until" is the plain English. Left.
- **‘furðum’ "just then".** Within the glossed range; the note offers the alternative. Left.
- **‘bēodgenēatas’ "table-companions".** Matches the ‘heorðgenēatas’ treatment in Fitt IV. Left; not proposed as a house row (does not obviously recur).
- **‘mōdsefa’ `l` "mind-spirit".** Consistent with the new note. Left.
- **Dropping the folio notes (338, 360).** Harmless and accurate; kept.
- **Fitt-03 234 "meeting-words" vs the conventions table.** Already in QUESTIONS.md; outside this part.
- **Unit boundaries and `t`.** Out of scope for this pass; not touched.

## Notable

- No new house renderings. Unit 348 and 360 follow the `maþelode` rows exactly.
- Glossary follow-up (not done here): ‘freân’ needs a genitive-singular reading broadened onto its entry; ‘mōton’ has no entry (novel form).
- ‘Tr.’ in Klaeber's apparatus is Trautmann, not Thorkelin (‘Thk.’). Fitt-03's note at 204 speaks of "the two 1787 Thorkelin transcripts" for a reading; that may deserve a look in that part's own review, but was not checked here.

# Pass 2

Fresh full pass over `units.json` (25 units, 320–370) in the same order (labels and positions, OE to `l`, `l` to `i`, remembered English, consistency), then every parse in `gloss.json` and every `known-forms.json` reading against the lines. `t` untouched (checked by script against the pre-pass file); both JSON files valid. Pass-1 edits introduced no new errors in `l`, `i` or `n`. Coverage re-checked by script with the reader's own `WORD_RE` and `wordKey`: all 217 distinct word forms in the 25 `t` fields have an entry, either in the existing glossary or in `gloss.json`; no novel entry duplicates an existing one; every `__broaden__` entry contains the old entry whole.

Totals: **high 0, medium 7, low 12.**

## Changes

### Medium

- **366 · gloss `getēoh` · medium.** Entry said "2nd singular subjunctive … deny, refuse", against the unit's note (imperative of ‘getēon’, "grant, give"; ‘wearne getēon’ "to grant a refusal") and against the form (no final -e; the imperative singular). Rewritten: imperative singular, "to draw, grant, bestow", ‘wearne getēon’ "to grant a refusal, i.e. to refuse", sense read from the parts. Done.
- **365/344/364 · gloss `mōton` · medium.** Entry was present in `gloss.json` (novel) but said "present or subjunctive". The subjunctive plural would be ‘mōten’. Now: plural present indicative, with the subjunctive form named. Done.
- **367 · gloss `glædman` · medium.** Flagged by the glosser. Entry called it an adjective, vocative, with no hedge, although Klaeber's apparatus offers ‘glæd man’ (two words) and ‘glædmōd’. Now "glad man, gracious one", vocative, the alternatives named, the sense called a guess. Unit 366's note already says as much. Done.
- **335 · gloss `elþēodịge` · medium.** "adjective used as noun": in the line it is an adjective agreeing with ‘men’ (as the unit note says). Now adjective, accusative plural masculine, strong. Done.
- **358/359 · gloss `freân` · medium.** Existing entry has only the dative; the unit (and its note) read a genitive depending on ‘eaxlum’. `__broaden__` entry added: old entry whole + " · frēa — of the lord (genitive singular, weak; Deniga freân …)". Done.
- **351 · gloss `frēan` · medium.** Not on the pass-1 list. Existing entry has genitive (God) and dative; in ‘frēan Scildinga frīnan wille’ it is the accusative object of ‘frīnan’. `__broaden__` entry added (accusative singular, weak). Done.
- **348 · gloss `wendla` · medium.** "Wendels (Vandals), a people of the north" stated an identification as fact; the unit note rightly calls it a guess. Now "a people whose identity is uncertain (perhaps the Vandals or the people of Vendel)". Done.

### Low

- **327 · n · low.** "‘gūðsearo gumena’ … a genitive plural that repeats ‘byrnan’" read as if the whole phrase were the genitive. Now ‘gumena’ is the genitive plural and the phrase repeats ‘byrnan’. Done.
- **328 · n · low.** "‘sǣmanna searo’ … a genitive plural beside ‘gāras’" likewise. Now ‘sǣmanna’ genitive plural, ‘searo’ nominative in apposition to ‘gāras’. Done.
- **356 · n · low.** "‘gedriht’ … is a dative with ‘mid’": the form is the same as the accusative (the glossary entry has "accusative singular") and ‘mid’ takes either. Now "the object of ‘mid’". Done.
- **361 · n · low.** "two editors (‘Klu.’ and ‘Holt.’)": ‘Klu. ix 188’ is a journal reference, not an edition. Now "two scholars". Done.
- **344 · gloss `sunu` · low.** The unit's note says the text should read as a dative; the existing entry has only the accusative. `__broaden__` entry added: dative singular in sense, form looks nominative/accusative, some editors print ‘suna’. Done.
- **gloss `geæhtlan` · low.** Flagged by the glosser. "oblique singular" was vague. Now "apparently a weak noun, probably genitive singular after wyrðe; the ending -an serves for several cases; sense a guess". Done.
- **gloss `grǣge` · low.** "feminine/masculine": it agrees with ‘syrcan’ (feminine). Now accusative plural feminine, strong. Done.
- **gloss `higeþrymm` · low.** "high spirit, courage" now "mind-might, high courage", matching `l` and the note. Done.
- **gloss `wulfgār` · low.** "a prince of the Wendels": the text says only ‘Wendla lēod’. Now "a man of the Wendels". Done.
- **gloss `wile` · low.** "also subjunctive": the subjunctive singular is ‘wille’. Now 3rd singular present indicative. Done.
- **gloss `wīggetāwum` · low.** Second element given as ‘tāwa’ "implement"; the unit's note and the word have ‘getāwa’ "equipment". Done.
- **gloss `ðē`, `ðū`, `recedes`, `anhār` · low.** Entries are meant to be general to the form: "here spelled" (ðē, ðū) and "of Heorot" (recedes) pinned them to a line; removed. `anhār` now says Klaeber's form is an emendation of the manuscript's ‘un hár’ (as the `þē` entry does for its emendation). Done.

## Parses checked and left

Every other `gloss.json` entry checked against its line(s) for case, number, tense, mood and lemma, and every `known-forms.json` entry (including the `__broaden__` ones from the glosser: `bēowulf`, `for`, `gūðsearo`, `hrōðgār`, `men`, `mīn`, `sele`, `syrcan`, `wine`, `ymb`, `æfter`, `þæs`, `þā`, `þē`, `þēoden`, `þǣm`) against its uses in this part; all cover their uses. Specific rechecks: ‘ōretmecgas’ (accusative at 332, nominative at 363; entry gives both); ‘sīð’ accusative; ‘searo’ and ‘gūðsearo’ nominative in apposition; ‘lēod’ nominative singular at 340, 348; ‘scīr’, ‘heard’, ‘hondlocen’ agreeing with their nouns at 322; ‘mōdiglīcran’ weak accusative plural with ‘men’; ‘wyrðe’ nominative plural; ‘dēah’ 3rd singular; ‘wēn’ elided first person.

## Considered and refused

- **Unit 340 note, "‘higerōf’ in Fitt III".** Searched the published text and found no ‘higerōf’ at first; Fitt III 204 prints ‘hige(r)ōfne’, so the reference stands. Kept.
- **`geæhtlan` as a certain genitive.** Cannot be settled from the line (‘wyrðe’ takes genitive, and the ending is ambiguous); kept hedged in the glossary, and the unit note already calls the sense a guess.
- **Unit 366 `getēoh` as a subjunctive.** The form has no -e and the prohibition with ‘nō’ takes the imperative; the unit was right, the glossary changed.
- **Unit 358 ‘Deniga freân’ as a dative.** Pass 1's genitive stands: ‘for’ already has the dative ‘eaxlum’.
- **‘mōton’ as a mood-dependent form in the `þæt` clauses.** Labelled present plural; no stronger claim.
- **Unit 327 "this habit of saying a thing twice is common in the poem".** A true general remark, not an aphorism about the story; kept.
- **Unit 340 `i` "spoke his answer" after "answered".** Doubles a little, but ‘word æfter spræc’ is a formula and the `l` carries the literal wording. Kept.
- **Unit 366 `i` "reply" for the plural ‘gegncwida’.** Natural English; `l` has "replies". Kept.
- **Unit 358 `i` "close before"** (pass 1). Kept.
- **House renderings.** None new; 348/360 follow the `maþelode` rows exactly.
- **Straight apostrophes in possessives** (Higelac's etc.): same as the published parts.

## Notable

- Follow-ups from pass 1 closed: ‘freân’ broadened (genitive), ‘mōton’ present in `gloss.json` and corrected.
- Cross-references to Fitts III and IV (lagustrǣte, ‘fāh ond fȳrheard’, scionon, wīsade/wīsige, receda, heorðgenēatas, ārstafum, ombeht, hwurfe, ‘word æfter cwæð’, geweorðad, se yldesta, wēne at 271, frēan Scyldinga) and the apparatus references (T.C. § 28, also § 23 at 395b; line 392 ‘ēower æþelu’) verified against the root files and the source.
